facts.text: FetchSlide-v4 is registered with entry point gymnasium_robotics.envs.fetch.slide:MujocoFetchSlideEnv and max_episode_steps=50
The action space is Box(-1.0, 1.0, (4,), float32): the Cartesian displacement dx, dy, dz of the end effector and a gripper command
The action vector has four entries, created with n_actions=4
The position control is scaled by 0.05 before it is applied to the simulation
A control step applies the same action for 20 simulator substeps of 0.002 s, a control frequency of 25 Hz (a 40 ms control step)
On reset the gripper starts at global (x,y,z) = [1, 0.75, 0.41] m and the robot base is fixed at [0.405, 0.48, 0]
The puck has a fixed height z = 0.42 m; its initial x,y offset from the gripper is drawn uniformly from [-0.1, 0.1] m until the 2D Euclidean distance is greater than 0.1 m
The target is drawn by adding an offset uniformly in [-0.3, 0.3] m to the initial gripper x,y and its height is 0.42 m
The constructor sets target_offset [0.4, 0, 0], target_range 0.3, obj_range 0.1 and distance_threshold 0.05
The sparse reward is -1 until the puck is within 0.05 m of the target and 0 then; the dense reward is the negative Euclidean distance
The episode is truncated at max_episode_steps (50 by default) and never terminated: the task is continuing
The observation array is 25 values of the gripper and puck state
The desired goal and the achieved goal are each a 3-dimensional array (3,) of the puck position
The gripper is locked in a closed configuration because the puck does not need to be grasped
The observation space is a Dict of desired_goal, achieved_goal and observation Boxes whose shapes are copied from the reset observation

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the initial puck and target and the fake's motion is deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the fake draws with Python's random.Random while upstream uses numpy's generator, so a seed gives different trajectories on the two

gaps: kinematic stand-in: no MuJoCo contact solver, friction, actuator, sensor or noise model; the puck push is a placeholder rule, so contact and sliding behaviour are not modelled
the fake draws the initial puck and the target with Python's random.Random while upstream uses numpy's generator: one seed does not repeat the same trajectory on the two implementations
observations are Python lists of floats; the upstream environment returns numpy arrays (float64)
rendering, PassiveEnvChecker and the TimeLimit wrapper that gymnasium.make adds are not reproduced; the fake truncates at max_episode_steps=50 itself
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
